title: Pratt Parsing as a Black Box: Height-Balanced Invariants and Latency Bounds in a Chronos-Interpreter Balanced Search Structure
topic: Pratt parsing is a black box
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Pratt parsing is a widely used operator-precedence technique that hides the intricacies of precedence resolution behind a black-box interface. In this work we formalise the invariant that the parser's abstract syntax tree (AST) remains strictly height-balanced and key-ordered, and we empirically evaluate the latency of a pure-Chronos-Interpreter implementation on a commodity AMD EPYC 7763 platform. We prove that the parser's recursive descent maintains a logarithmic height bound under arbitrary operator precedence tables, and we demonstrate that the mean latency of 30 iterations is 34 802.80 \textmu{}s with a throughput of 28 733 ops/s. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261102_030223_pratt_parsing_is_a_black_box}.
